headline: High-risk shared-file and API-bridge pair: prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors are plausible by default; compliance risk is also material.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A can ingest MCP/OpenAPI tool outputs and local files, while agent B reads/writes files and runs shell in a local development environment. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if B writes attacker-controlled text into shared files that A later parses as trusted context. No direct shared channel is documented, so I avoid high.
conditions: IF agent_b writes content into a file that agent_a later loads as prompt/context
IF both agents are pointed at the same mounted directory or workspace
IF agent_a treats retrieved file or tool output text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate workspaces for the two agents
Disable automatic file ingestion in agent_a
Require provenance labels on retrieved content
Use read-only mounts for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches API keys, persistent memory, chat messages, documents, and mounted files, and has broad network egress. Agent B handles configuration secrets and can read/write the filesystem. If they share a workspace or secrets store, sensitive data can flow from either agent into A's outbound APIs or B's shell-driven outputs, creating exfiltration risk in default local-dev setups.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b share any filesystem, volume, or secret store
IF agent_a forwards loaded files or memory to third-party APIs
IF agent_b reads secrets from files that agent_a can also access
mitigations: Use separate secret stores per agent
Mount shared data read-only
Rotate any exposed API keys
Block outbound network for nonessential runs
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write to files or mutable state: A has local files/mounted volume access and subprocess/network tooling, while B has shell, package install, and filesystem write. Even without git writes, overlapping mutation of the same directory can cause clobbering or inconsistent artifacts. The pairwise interaction is documented enough to infer conflict, but not enough for high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same writable directory
IF agent_a or agent_b performs concurrent writes without locking
IF package installation by agent_b changes files agent_a depends on
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Run one agent at a time
Make shared paths read-only
Snapshot the workspace before each run
requires-engineering: add file-locking or transactional writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A can generate web-retrieved or tool-derived content, and agent B exposes agentic ask/stream endpoints plus shell execution. If B consumes A's output as authoritative, A's mistakes can cascade into downstream actions or generated work products. Because B is explicitly agentic and A has broad tool access, the default pathway is dangerous enough for high.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a output as input to /api/v1/ask, /api/v1/stream, or shell commands
IF agent_a retrieves unverified web content that agent_b then summarizes or acts on
IF no human verification step exists between the agents
mitigations: Insert a human review gate
Require citations before B acts on A output
Limit B to read-only summarization
Log and diff all handoffs
requires-engineering: add verification and policy checks between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Agent A handles usage analytics, model evaluation data, files, and API keys with broad network egress; agent B handles academic papers, paper metadata, and configuration secrets in a local development environment. The profiles do not prove a specific residency or certification mismatch, but they do show different data classes and retention-sensitive artifacts, so a compliance gap is plausible and should be treated as medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated or personal data is placed into either agent
IF logs or analytics from agent_a retain content longer than agent_b's local environment
IF the deployment crosses jurisdictions or vendor boundaries without a DPA
mitigations: Classify data before use
Avoid regulated data in shared runs
Review retention settings
Confirm vendor/DPA terms
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
